values.value: Notes on why the Model Context Protocol is changing how agents connect to the world.
A short blog about MCP — the Model Context Protocol — and why it is quietly becoming the way agents meet the world.

value.markup: Welcome. This little site exists to make one argument: the Model Context Protocol is one of the most quietly important ideas in software right now. Below you will find two posts on why — and room for more as the story develops.

values.value: What Is MCP and Why It Is Awesome
An introduction to the Model Context Protocol and why its open, simple design matters.
The Model Context Protocol gives AI agents a single, open way to talk to tools and data — and that simplicity is exactly what makes it powerful.
What Is MCP and Why It Is Awesome
One open standard, endlessly many tools.

value.markup:
Before the Model Context Protocol, connecting an AI assistant to a new data source meant writing a custom integration for every pairing: one adapter for the calendar, another for the database, another for the file system. The combinatorics explode. With N tools and M assistants you can end up maintaining N times M bespoke connectors.

MCP replaces that mess with a single open protocol. Any tool can expose itself once as an MCP server, and any agent can speak MCP as a client. The result is the same kind of network effect that made USB universal: build one device, and it plugs into everything.

values.value: Every tool speaks one protocol — like traces on a circuit board. Photo: Alexandre Debiève / Unsplash.
Macro photograph of a black circuit board with fine copper traces
It is the USB-C port for AI applications.
The metaphor that launched a thousand MCP servers

value.markup:
That USB-C metaphor captures what makes MCP awesome: it is boring in the best way. It does not compete with the models; it just standardizes the socket. An open spec, reference SDKs in popular languages, and a design that treats tools, resources, and prompts as first-class primitives make it easy to adopt and easy to trust.

When a protocol is this simple, the ecosystem grows itself — and that is the real payoff.

values.value: MCP in Practice: Five Reasons Agents Love It
Five practical reasons the Model Context Protocol has become the standard way agents connect to tools.
From one-line server launches to secure, composable tool access, MCP earns its keep in real deployments — here are five reasons why.
MCP in Practice: Five Reasons Agents Love It
What the protocol looks like once it leaves the slide deck.

value.markup:
Theory is nice, but a protocol earns its reputation in deployment. Here are five reasons teams keep choosing MCP once they try it in anger.

1. One standard, many clients. Write your server once and every MCP-speaking agent can use it.

2. Composability. Tools, resources, and prompts compose cleanly, so agents can chain capabilities without bespoke glue code.

3. Security boundaries. Servers declare what they expose; clients mediate access, so permissions are explicit rather than implicit.

4. Ecosystem momentum. Thousands of community servers already exist, from databases to design tools.

5. It is boring on purpose. The spec stays small, which makes audits, tests, and long-term maintenance realistic.
